newsitem.title: USA: Domino's Pizza plans 300 new stores in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Domino's Pizza plans 300 new stores in 1997.

text.p: Domino's Pizza Inc., which operates 5,560 stores in 54 countries markets, said Friday it will open 300 stores in 1997, mostly in international markets.
"Three hundred is our goal again in 1997, about 250 in international markets and 50 in the U.S.," said Tim McIntyre, vice president of corporate relations.
"In international markets, there is plenty of opportunity for us," he said in a telephone interview from the company's headquarters in Ann Arbor, Mich.

Domino's opened more than 300 new stores in 1996 and ended the year with 5,560 stores. Most of the new stores opened in international markets, as Domino's entered nine new countries including Greece, India, Turkey and Scotland.
It will open its second store in Beijing next week. Domino's largest international markets, Mexico and Japan, have about 150 stores.

Domino's reported its 1996 worldwide gross sales rose more than 10 percent over a year ago to more than $2.8 billion. The company also reported record pre-tax profits for 1996 of $50.6 million, up 36 percent from 1995.

Same store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, in the United States increased nearly 7 percent while same store sales in the company's international units were up over 5 percent. Gross sales for the company's international units exceeded $500 million for the first time, the company said in March.

Domino's said its financial results improved from a company decision in 1992 to abandon diversification projects. These included introducing submarine sandwiches and salads, using alternative methods of distribution, and co-branding its pizzas.

"We believe the return to focusing on our core business -- pizza delivery -- coupled with great new products and strong international growth accounted for our tremendous results in 1996, Harry Silverman, Domino's chief financial officer, said in a statement.

Domino's said its national advertising budget for 1997 will remain at about $75 million, even with last year, with expenditures covering both print and broadcast media. Local markets again will contribute an additional $35 million.
